title: Resuming one of two parallel interrupts inside a subgraph re-runs a sibling node that already completed
observed_behavior: A child subgraph has two parallel nodes, each calling interrupt() before a side effect. Resuming the two interrupts one at a time, each by its own id, produces the correct final log but the node completed first runs its side effect twice: runs == {'a': 2, 'b': 1} instead of {'a': 1, 'b': 1}.
structure_focus: Parallel interrupts inside a compiled subgraph; per-interrupt-id resume and replay of already-completed sibling tasks
notes: Closed (fixed by #9315, per last comment); labels bug/external. Side-effect counters make the duplicate execution visible even though final state is correct. Issue traces it to PregelLoop.is_replaying being true for every nested graph because task configs carry checkpoint_id=None; the candidate fix clears is_replaying for nested non-time-traveling runs. Fixture keeps the one-at-a-time resume loop and the counter assertions.
